answer: The planker fits each strake of planks by hand and counts the planks in his tally, so the hull is proved planked strake by strake. A relic strake claimed as fitted fails the tally: the planks must match the hull's own curve at the meadow of the fitting, and a strake never fitted leaves a gap in the side. Buying a false plank record costs a forger 10,700 in bribes to the planker and fees to the yard, and the plume tally is checked at every inspection, so a hull whose planks were never fitted leaks at the first tide.
